terms.gloss: the casing round a door or window; a window frame
evidence: Vitr. 4.6: Ipsa autem antepagmenta contrahantur in summō suae crassitūdinis XIIII parte
terms.comment: A builder’s word: the wooden or stone casing fixed round a door or a window (Lewis & Short: “ornaments about the doors, windows”). Cato lists it among the woodwork the builder must make for a new farmhouse. Of a window, say antepagmenta fenestrae; usually plural.

phrases.english: The window frames aren’t fixed in yet.

phrases.latin: Vīllam aedificandam sī locābis novam ab solō, faber haec faciat oportet … līmina, postēs … fenestrās … antepagmenta
phrases.english: If you contract for a new farmhouse to be built from the ground up, the builder must make these things: … sills, doorposts, … windows, … casings
